An Akwa Ibom-born computer engineering graduate who emerged as the University of Uyo’s overall best graduating student, Abasifreke Nkanang has credited an Oriental Energy Resources scholarship with helping him concentrate on his studies and achieve a 4.91 cumulative grade point average (CGPA).
Mr Nkanang’s achievement at the university’s 31st and 32nd combined convocation shows the impact of corporate-funded education support, particularly for students who might otherwise struggle to meet the financial demands of university education.
According to a report by Punch, Mr Nkanang attributed his academic success to discipline, goal-setting and focus. He said the scholarship he received from Oriental Energy Resources Limited helped him concentrate on his studies.
The university’s Vice-Chancellor, Christopher Ekong , celebrated Mr Nkanang’s achievement, describing it as outstanding and a source of pride to the institution.
Speaking at the convocation on Thursday, Mr Ekong, a professor, said Mr Nkanang’s performance proved the value of diligence and commitment to academic excellence.
“Nkanang’s achievement is clear evidence of diligence, discipline and commitment to academic excellence,” the vice-chancellor said.
Mr Nkanang, speaking after the ceremony, said having a clear academic target from his first year was central to his success.

“When you come to school, set up a goal that you want to achieve for yourself. If it is academics, aim for the high echelon of graduates,” he advised other students.
The Head of Community Relations at Oriental Energy Resources, Uwem Ite , said the company was particularly pleased that a beneficiary of its scholarship scheme emerged as the university’s best graduating student.
He said the company, which operates offshore in Akwa Ibom, established the scholarship programme as part of its corporate social responsibility to support university students from the state.
“The overall best graduating student of this convocation was a beneficiary of that scholarship, and he read engineering. Our financial support really enabled him to get to the point that he is now,” Mr Ite said.
The company’s education programme provides merit-based scholarships for secondary and tertiary education to high-achieving students from its host communities. The awards cover tuition fees for the duration of beneficiaries’ academic programmes.
According to information on the company’s website, Oriental Energy has awarded scholarships to 470 beneficiaries and makes 50 new awards annually.
The scholarship initiative is part of the company’s interventions in education. In 2012, the company also supported the University of Uyo’s efforts to secure full accreditation for its chemical and petroleum engineering departments by funding renovations, equipment and departmental libraries.
Mr Nkanang’s achievement came during the university’s 31st and 32nd combined convocation, which covered the 2023/2024 and 2024/2025 academic sessions.
The university graduated 22,961 students, including 214 who earned first-class honours.
For his academic distinction, Mr Nkanang received a N500,000 prize from the vice-chancellor. Wema Bank also awarded him N2.5 million, while the university’s chancellor gave him N300,000.
